assumptions.assumption: The client component that today owns the year and title filter state is `components/changelog/ChangelogFilteredList.tsx` and is the correct place to add URL-sync logic. If the file lives elsewhere or is named differently, the touches and test entry points should be adjusted accordingly without changing the behaviour specified here.

The title-search match is case-insensitive substring today; this spec keeps that behaviour. If the current match is exact or case-sensitive, AC2 pins case-insensitive substring as the intended behaviour.

The year filter control offers a single-select of years (with an 'all years' option). If it is a multi-select, ?year= would need to accept a repeated or comma-separated value and this spec would need extension.

The changelog page (`app/changelog/page.tsx`) is a server component that passes entries to a client filter component; URL parsing therefore happens client-side via `useSearchParams`. Pre-rendering the filtered set server-side from `searchParams` is not required for this change.

clarified_description: The changelog's year filter and title search currently live in component state only: a reader who has narrowed the list has a view they cannot share (a link goes to the unfiltered list), and a page reload discards the narrowing. This change moves both filters into the URL query string under `?year=` and `?q=`, so a filtered view is shareable, bookmarkable, and reload-safe. The URL is the source of truth on load; user interaction with either filter updates the URL using replace (not push) so the browser Back button leaves `/changelog` rather than stepping through every keystroke or year change. An absent, empty (`?q=`), or whitespace-only parameter means 'no filter'. An unknown `?year` value (non-numeric, or numeric with no matching entry) is ignored — the full list renders — rather than an empty list. Both parameters combine when both are present. The RSS feed at `/changelog.xml` is not affected by these parameters.

constraints.detail: URL updates on every keystroke must use history.replaceState (via next/navigation router.replace) rather than pushState, so the history stack does not accumulate one entry per character.
The RSS route at /changelog.xml is a separate route and must not observe or honour these parameters; its output is a fixed feed.
Values must be URL-encoded when written and URL-decoded when read; the round-trip must be lossless for the character set typically found in entry titles (spaces, punctuation, unicode).

contracts.definition: URL contract for `/changelog`: two optional query parameters, `year` (integer as a string, e.g. `2025`) and `q` (free text, URL-encoded). Absent, empty, or whitespace-only values mean 'no filter'. Unknown `year` values are ignored. Both may appear together. No other parameters are consumed.

deferred_decisions: Whether year-selection URL encoding should support future extensions (multi-year, ranges) is out of scope. If the year filter is ever changed to multi-select, the query parameter shape will need to be extended and this spec re-visited.

Whether to debounce the `?q=` URL write (e.g. 100ms) is left to the engineer. The spec requires replace-not-push and matching-on-every-keystroke behaviour; if debouncing the URL write (while still filtering the list live) is a cleaner implementation for a given router version, that is acceptable provided the observable behaviour (final URL matches final input, back-navigation is a single hop) is unchanged.

flows.title: Filter ↔ URL sync

must: WHEN a visitor opens /changelog with ?year=<value> the system shall set the year filter to that value on load and shall render only entries whose year matches.

WHEN a visitor opens /changelog with ?q=<value> the system shall populate the title search input with that value on load and shall render only entries whose title contains the value as a case-insensitive substring.
WHEN a visitor opens /changelog with both ?year and ?q the system shall apply both filters together, rendering only entries that match both.
IF a query parameter is absent, empty, or contains only whitespace THEN the system shall treat that parameter as no filter.
IF the ?year value is non-numeric, or is numeric but matches no entry year, THEN the system shall ignore it and render all entries.
WHEN a visitor changes the year filter control the system shall update the URL query string to reflect the new value using history replace (not push).
WHEN a visitor types in the title search input the system shall update the URL query string to reflect the new value using history replace (not push).
WHEN a visitor clears the year filter the system shall remove the ?year parameter from the URL rather than leaving a bare ?year= behind.
WHEN a visitor clears the title search input the system shall remove the ?q parameter from the URL rather than leaving a bare ?q= behind.
WHILE any filter is applied the system shall reflect the filtered entry count in the on-page count indicator (the count already shown below the page heading).
WHEN the applied filters match no entries the system shall render an empty result region rather than the full unfiltered list.
The system shall leave the RSS feed at /changelog.xml unchanged in content and shape regardless of query-string parameters on /changelog.

non_functional.why_not: filtering runs client-side over a small in-memory list already loaded on the page; URL-sync work per keystroke is O(1) string composition.
no new dependency, network call, or server path is introduced.
query parameters are user-supplied filter values (year, free-text search terms) and carry no PII in the intended usage; the values were already held in component state.
no server-side handling changes; no new logs or metrics are added.

non_functional.target: the year filter and title search remain keyboard-navigable and screen-reader announced exactly as they are today; label associations are preserved.

non_functional.why_not: no regulated data or process is involved.

open_questions: The exact filenames of the year-filter and title-search components under `components/changelog/` were not observed directly — the touches list is based on the conventional name `ChangelogFilteredList`. If this is wrong the engineer should update paths without changing behaviour.
outcome: A reader who has narrowed the changelog to a year, a search term, or both can share the URL and have the recipient see the same view — and can refresh the page without losing the filter.
rationale:
**Why the URL is the source of truth, not component state kept in sync with the URL.** Two mechanisms competing to own the same value is where filter-sync bugs live (a keystroke that races a back-navigation, an initial render that reads state before the URL is parsed). Reading `useSearchParams()` on every render and deriving the visible filter from it keeps one source of truth. On user input, we write to the URL and let the re-render pick up the new value.

**Why replace rather than push.** The description called this out and it is the right call: typing 'firebase' pushes six history entries otherwise, and back-navigation from the changelog takes six presses to leave. Replace keeps back-navigation intuitive at the cost of not being able to step through prior filter states — a fair trade for a filter UI. The year change is also replace for symmetry: a shared link with `?year=2025` should look like arriving on that view, not like arriving on the default view and then changing the filter.

**Why empty and whitespace-only are 'no filter'.** A shared link with a stray `&q=` on the end, or a filter cleared then re-shared, should not behave differently from the unfiltered page. Similarly, whitespace-only search would match every entry anyway (trim before non-empty check), so treating it as 'no filter' is both cleaner and observably identical for matching, with the added benefit that the URL is cleaned up.

**Why unknown year renders all, not none.** A shared link that grows stale (year no longer present in the data) or a hand-typed URL with a typo should degrade to 'full list' rather than 'empty result'. An empty result reads like the changelog has nothing to show, which is misleading; the full list is the safe default and the reader can see immediately that their filter did not take.

**Why RSS is untouched.** The feed is a fixed representation of all entries, consumed by aggregators that do not send query strings. Applying filters to it would silently change what a subscriber pulls; leaving it alone is the boring choice.

risks.mitigation: AC9 asserts that `router.push` is never called and that `router.replace` receives the final URL. A regression to push-per-keystroke fails the test.
risks.title: Every-keystroke URL write pushes to history if replace is misconfigured

risks.mitigation: Do not use `useState` initialised from `useSearchParams`; derive filter values on every render from `useSearchParams()`. AC1 and AC2 fail if initial paint reads local state that is empty until effect-hydration.
risks.title: URL becomes the source of truth on subsequent renders, but initial paint reads stale state

risks.mitigation: AC6 (non-numeric) and AC7 (numeric-but-unknown) both assert the full list renders. Both are exercised in the test suite.
risks.title: Unknown year silently blanks the list rather than falling back to all

risks.mitigation: AC10 and AC11 assert the parameters are removed, not left with an empty value; both are tested.
risks.title: Bare `?q=` or `?year=` re-appears after clear

should: WHEN the URL contains a ?q value with URL-encoded characters (spaces, punctuation) the system shall decode the value before matching, so that a shared link matches the same entries as the input that produced it.

standards_applied.why_not: every acceptance criterion in this spec is covered by a test in acceptance_tests[]; there is no uncovered criterion for this standard to govern.
no customer-facing copy is added or modified; only two URL parameters are read and written.

swe_constraints: Use `useSearchParams()` and `useRouter()` from `next/navigation` (Next.js 16 App Router). Read `AGENTS.md` at repo root — the note about Next.js breaking changes applies; consult `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` for the current router API before writing code.
Use `router.replace(pathname + '?' + params.toString(), { scroll: false })` rather than `router.push` for every URL update. `scroll: false` prevents the page jumping to the top on a filter change.

Do not maintain a parallel `useState` for filter values in addition to reading `useSearchParams`. Deriving from search params on each render is the single source of truth; a mirror in state re-introduces the sync bug this feature exists to remove.
When writing the URL, omit parameters whose value is empty or whitespace-only. Do not emit `?q=` or `?year=` with an empty value.
Trim the `q` value before matching. Preserve the original (trimmed) casing in the input display; lowercase both sides only for the comparison.
For the year filter: parse the `?year` value with `Number.parseInt(v, 10)`. Reject `NaN` and any value not present in the derived set of entry years — treat both as 'no filter'.
For character-safety on the wire, use `URLSearchParams` (which handles encoding) rather than string concatenation.
Do not add any dependency to satisfy this change. `next/navigation` and `URLSearchParams` are sufficient.

criteria: The URL updates as I change filters
Opening a URL with ?year and/or ?q pre-populates the controls and filters the list on load
Pressing the browser Back button once takes me off /changelog, not through my typing history
user_stories.so_that: I can share, bookmark, and reload a filtered view without losing it
user_stories.want: the year I've selected and the search text I've typed to be reflected in the URL

jobs_to_be_done: Point a colleague at a specific set of changelog entries (e.g. 'everything about Firebase in 2025')
Bookmark a filtered view for quick return
Refresh the page mid-read without losing their place
users.name: Changelog reader sharing a specific view
pain_points: The URL always looks like /changelog; there is nothing to copy that preserves the filter
A reload snaps back to the full unfiltered list
Back-navigation walks through every keystroke of the search — six presses to leave a page after typing 'fire'

wont: The system will not auto-focus the search input on load when a query parameter is present — a shared link is opened to be read, not edited.
The system will not persist filters across separate visits by any mechanism other than the URL (no cookies, no localStorage).
The system will not introduce query parameters beyond ?year and ?q; no pagination, sort, or category parameters are added.
The system will not change the RSS feed to accept or honour these parameters.
